**Step 5 Preview on Nous Portal:** The section's lead is **@NousResearch**'s announcement that **StepFun**'s [**Step 5 Preview** is free on **Nous Portal** for a week](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-6433f2551b93) — a **600B-total / 27B-active** MoE with **1M context** and vision, pulling 35k views. **Hermes Agent typo saga:** The viral moment of the week — the official account's garbled '[**Hemres Agnet**](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-bb8ca524b286)' post (**2267 likes**), widely read as an accidental early reveal of **Hermes Agent**. **@Teknium** teased ['drunk again i see'](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-e5c96aa97188) and the official account [fired back 'sleep deprived'](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-4a9fe96b12cd), while cryptic follow-ups (['**it's agnetic**'](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-4d38d340e483), ['**it's two words**'](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-7249d38c72fb), and Teknium's ['**it's coming fren**'](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-8774a4bbb986)) converted the typo into a de facto release teaser. Sentiment is amused and hyped; the community broadly reads the thread as confirmation something new is imminent, which is high-value material for a Hermes-focused newsletter despite the low-content posts themselves.

**Official banter & community health:** A long tail of emoji and one-word replies from **@Teknium** and **@NousResearch** — the ['why tag us if we don't exist'](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-a4796bd36edb) running joke (231 likes), [contributor shout-outs to **@andrexibiza**](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-fcb4462f8487), and a [salute to **@HermesAgentTips**](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-3f33e2d5e206) — carries little information but reflects an unusually chatty, high-touch official presence and warm sentiment toward contributors. Buried in the banter is one real signal: a [pending **OpenAI Devs**-compatibility change ('if not will get it in')](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-47891ae03e98).

**Local model preferences:** Practical [community advice favors **GLM 5.3** or **DeepSeek 4.1 Flash** for local serving on **Blackwell** GPUs](/?date=2026-10-10&category=social#item-807e70987e02) — a small but genuinely useful data point showing where open-model users are landing. The remaining bottom-half posts (emoji-only replies, bare 'yes/no' answers with no context) were excluded as newsletter noise.
